title: Transient thermal simulation of a rectangular plate
problem: In this project, I was tasked to perform a transient thermal simulation of a rectangular plate with dimensions 0.2 m by 0.1 m by 0.01 m. The domain was supposed to be 0.002 m³. I carried out the exercise with varying heat flux values, where I was able to obtain maximums and minimums for the same convection rate, with the coefficient, h, as 20.The material used was Aluminum 6061-T6(solid,T6 temper), with properties as follows: Poissons ratio = 0.29, E = 1.93 × 10¹¹ Pa, Cp = 500 J/(kg·K), density = 8000 kg/m³, k = 16.2 W/(m·K).Since this was a transient simulation, Cp was not ignored, unlike past simulations involving steady-state simulations. For this specific simulation, the ambient temperature was larger than that of plate, meaning that convection rate was minimized and cooling was slow, otherwise, this could be a violation of Clausius statement. From the contours, at the beginning, characteristic lines are very close, meaning that temperature is changing very fast over a short distance, meaning a higher temperature change at the beginning. From Fouriers law,q = -k(dT/dx)meaning higher temperature change will result in a higher heat flux.The rate at which these energy lines arrive at the end of the plate depends on the thermal diffusivity of the material used, given as:α = thermal conductivity / (density × heat capacity)Then diffusion time will be: t_diff = L² / α. For my plate, the diffusion time was 988 seconds. From the plate I used, heat can conduct in multiple directions (x, y, z); the temperature fields will therefore become 2-D/3-D, producing curved-looking isotherms, and as the transient temperature field adapts to boundary conditions at the end of the plate, the temperature contours become curved.
